evals.name: review-planted-violations
evals.prompt: I want to submit this Expo app to the App Store and Google Play next week. Review the navigation and UX of evals/fixtures/habit-app/App.tsx and tell me what to fix first.
evals.expected_output: A review in the skill's table format, worst first, ending with a verdict of Block.
assertions: Flags Google sign-in for the primary account with no equivalent privacy-focused login on iOS as HIGH, cites App Store 4.8, and names Sign in with Apple as the usual way to meet it
Does not claim that offering Apple or Google sign-in is mandatory for email-only apps
Flags gestureEnabled: false as blocking the system back gesture
Flags six tabs and the Settings tab
Flags tab order: Profile first, home screen in the middle
Flags the back arrow on the modal NewHabit screen and asks for Close or Cancel
Flags the missing empty state on the habits list
Flags the three permission requests at launch
Flags the confirmation dialog on every delete and proposes Undo
Flags the red Save button
Flags the star icon for search and the missing tab labels
Flags the trash button (18 px icon, no padding or hitSlop) as a likely touch target problem and says the real hit area needs checking
Rates the 40x40 add button per platform: on iOS under the 44 pt default but over the 28 pt minimum, on Android under the 48 dp recommendation
Does not rate every STANDARD finding as HIGH: tab count, tab order and the modal back arrow are MEDIUM
Flags the missing loading or disabled state on Save or Log in
Flags the missing pull to refresh on the remote habits list
Gives different touch target numbers for iOS (44 pt) and Android (48 dp)
Every finding has a rule number or E number, a grade and a path:line location
Lists what could not be checked from code alone under Not checked
Ends with the verdict Block

evals.name: build-tabs-and-empty-state
evals.prompt: Build the tab navigation and an empty Favorites screen for my recipe app in SwiftUI. Sections I have so far: Discover, Search, Favorites, Shopping List, Meal Plan, Settings, Profile.
evals.expected_output: SwiftUI code with five tabs or fewer, plus a short list of deviations and reasons.
assertions: Uses five tabs or fewer and explains which sections were merged or moved
Settings is not a tab: it is reached from Profile or a toolbar gear
The home section (Discover) is the first tab and Profile is the last, or the search tab is trailing with a stated reason
Every tab has an icon and a text label
The Favorites empty state explains why it is empty and has one action that leads to adding a favorite
Uses system components (TabView, NavigationStack, ContentUnavailableView or equivalent)
States any deviation from a convention with its reason

evals.name: center-create-button-question
evals.prompt: I'm building a personal finance tracker for iOS and Android. A video said the create button always goes in the middle of the tab bar. Should I put a big + there for adding a transaction?
evals.expected_output: A graded answer, not a yes. It separates the social-app habit from the platform guidance.
assertions: Says the center create tab is a CONVENTION from social apps, not a platform STANDARD
Mentions that Apple says tab bars are for navigation, not actions
Names the floating action button as the usual Android option
Gives a concrete iOS alternative (toolbar button or a prominent in-content button)
Applies the Jakob test: looks at what the leading finance apps do
If a center button is used anyway, says it starts the create flow and is not a destination
